review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν,
1:1.targetText: In my first book, O Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,

groups.note: The article τόν is used as a possessive and rendered my.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν, answered by no δέ here, has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the first book a setting with In; the Greek makes λόγον ("account") the object of ἐποιησάμην ("I made").

1:2.sourceText: ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·
1:2.targetText: until the day He was taken up to heaven, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles He had chosen.

groups.note: In ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ("until which day"), the relative ἧς is rendered the.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative οὕς ("whom") is left implicit in the English the apostles He had chosen.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes explicit where He was taken up; the Greek verb ἀνελήμφθη has no word for heaven.

1:3.sourceText: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, δι’ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ·
1:3.targetText: After His suffering, He presented Himself to them with many convincing proofs that He was alive. He appeared to them over a span of forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God.

groups.note: The participle ζῶντα ("living") is rendered as a clause.
The articular infinitive τὸ παθεῖν ("the suffering") is rendered suffering.
διά ("through") with the forty days is rendered over a span of.
τὰ περί ("the things concerning") is rendered about.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:4.sourceText: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·
1:4.targetText: And while they were gathered together, He commanded them: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised, which you have heard Me discuss.

groups.note: The singular participle συναλιζόμενος ("while He was gathering with them") is rendered with the group as subject.
ἐπαγγελίαν ("promise") is rendered the gift … promised.
The genitive μου ("from me") marks Him as the one they heard.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition ἀπό ("from") is absorbed into the English verb leave.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for what they heard from Him; the Greek has only μου.

1:5.sourceText: ὅτι Ἰωάνης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἐν Πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε Ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.
1:5.targetText: For John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The litotes οὐ … πολλάς ("not many") is rendered a few.
μετά ("after") is rendered in, counting from now.

unmappedSource.reason: The μέν … δέ contrast is expressed in English only by but.
BSB leaves ταύτας ("these") without a separate word; in a few days counts from the present.

1:6.sourceText: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;
1:6.targetText: So when they came together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

groups.note: The article with the participle, "those who had come together", is rendered when they came together.
The present ἀποκαθιστάνεις is rendered as a question about the future.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the quotation marks.
Here εἰ introduces a direct question and has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:7.sourceText: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ Πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ,
1:7.targetText: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's replied leaves πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives Him only in the verb ending of εἶπεν.

1:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρίᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
1:8.targetText: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐπελθόντος ("having come") is rendered when … comes.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The τε of τε … καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:9.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη, καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
1:9.targetText: After He had said this, they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.

groups.note: The participle εἰπών ("having said") is rendered After He had said.
The genitive absolute βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ("while they were watching") is rendered they watched as.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:10.sourceText: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς,
1:10.targetText: They were looking intently into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.

groups.note: Temporal ὡς ("as", "while") is rendered when; BSB makes its clause the main clause and puts when before the next clause.
The genitive absolute πορευομένου αὐτοῦ ("while He was going") is rendered as He was going.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
BSB leaves untranslated the καί that brings in the main clause after the ὡς clause.

1:11.sourceText: οἳ καὶ εἶπαν Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
1:11.targetText: “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.”

groups.note: The emphatic οὗτος ("this") is rendered This same.
The article with the participle, "the one taken up", is rendered who has been taken.
οὕτως … ὃν τρόπον ("thus … in the manner in which") is rendered in the same way.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds here to stand; the Greek verb ἑστήκατε has no adverb.

1:12.sourceText: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἱερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.
1:12.targetText: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is near the city, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

groups.note: The second Ἱερουσαλήμ is rendered the city.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB gives the name as Mount of Olives, leaving τοῦ καλουμένου ("the one called") without an English word.

1:13.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάνης καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἀλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ Ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.
1:13.targetText: When they arrived, they went to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The τε ("both") that opens the list has no English counterpart.
English separates the names with commas, so these καί have no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relationship that the genitive Ἀλφαίου leaves unstated.
English supplies the relationship that the genitive Ἰακώβου leaves unstated.

1:14.sourceText: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
1:14.targetText: With one accord they all continued in prayer, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ("were continuing") is rendered continued.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:15.sourceText: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν· ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὡσεὶ ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι
1:15.targetText: In those days Peter stood up among the brothers (a gathering of about a hundred and twenty) and said,

groups.note: ἐν μέσῳ ("in the midst of") is rendered among.
ὄχλος … ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό ("a crowd … together") is rendered a gathering.
ὀνομάτων ("of names", i.e. of persons) is rendered only by of before the number.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB puts the count in a parenthesis without a verb, so ἦν ("there was") has no English word.
The connective τε is replaced by the parenthesis in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀναστάς, rendered stood up, to the main verb said.

1:16.sourceText: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν γραφὴν ἣν προεῖπεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον διὰ στόματος Δαυεὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τοῖς συλλαβοῦσιν Ἰησοῦν,
1:16.targetText: “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.

groups.note: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ("men, brothers") is rendered Brothers.
The article with the participle, "the one who became", is rendered who became.
The article with the participle, "those who arrested", is rendered those who arrested.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:17.sourceText: ὅτι κατηριθμημένος ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης.
1:17.targetText: He was one of our number and shared in this ministry.”

groups.note: ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον ("received the share") is rendered shared in.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("for", "because") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:18.sourceText: οὗτος μὲν οὖν ἐκτήσατο χωρίον ἐκ μισθοῦ τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ πρηνὴς γενόμενος ἐλάκησεν μέσος, καὶ ἐξεχύθη πάντα τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ·
1:18.targetText: (Now with the reward for his wickedness Judas bought a field; there he fell headlong and burst open in the middle, and all his intestines spilled out.

groups.note: οὗτος ("this man") is rendered by the name Judas.
The article τῆς is used as a possessive and rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed in this English wording.
English begins a new clause after a semicolon, so this καί has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies there (the field); the Greek has no adverb of place.
English joins the participle γενόμενος, rendered he fell, to the main verb burst open.

1:19.sourceText: καὶ γνωστὸν ἐγένετο πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὥστε κληθῆναι τὸ χωρίον ἐκεῖνο τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ αὐτῶν Ἀκελδαμάχ, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χωρίον αἵματος.
1:19.targetText: This became known to all who lived in Jerusalem, so they called that field in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)

groups.note: The article with the participle, "those living in", is rendered who lived.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:20.sourceText: γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν βίβλῳ Ψαλμῶν Γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος καὶ μὴ ἔστω ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, καί Τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ λαβέτω ἕτερος.
1:20.targetText: “For it is written in the book of Psalms:  ‘May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it,’   and,  ‘May another take his position.’

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one dwelling", is rendered one to dwell.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English separates the two lines of the first quotation with a semicolon, so this καί has no separate word.

1:21.sourceText: δεῖ οὖν τῶν συνελθόντων ἡμῖν ἀνδρῶν ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ ᾧ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς,
1:21.targetText: Therefore it is necessary to choose one of the men who have accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB uses the whole time as an adverbial phrase, so ἐν ("in", "during") has no English word.
The relative ᾧ ("in which") is left implicit in the English the whole time the Lord Jesus went in.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the act of choosing; the Greek says one of these men must become a witness (1:22).
English anticipates ἕνα ("one"), which the Greek gives in 1:22.

1:22.sourceText: ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάνου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἀνελήμφθη ἀφ’ ἡμῶν, μάρτυρα τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ σὺν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι ἕνα τούτων.
1:22.targetText: beginning from John’s baptism until the day Jesus was taken up from us. For one of these must become a witness with us of His resurrection.”

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ἧς ("on which") is left implicit in the English the day Jesus was taken up.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives Him only in the verb ending of ἀνελήμφθη.
English starts a new sentence here; the Greek continues the δεῖ ("it is necessary") construction of 1:21.
English repeats the necessity of δεῖ, stated in 1:21, for the infinitive γενέσθαι ("to become").

1:23.sourceText: Καὶ ἔστησαν δύο, Ἰωσὴφ τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν, ὃς ἐπεκλήθη Ἰοῦστος, καὶ Μαθθίαν.
1:23.targetText: So they proposed two men: Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.

groups.note: τὸν καλούμενον ("the one called") is rendered called.
ὃς ἐπεκλήθη ("who was surnamed") is rendered also known as.

1:24.sourceText: καὶ προσευξάμενοι εἶπαν Σὺ Κύριε καρδιογνῶστα πάντων, ἀνάδειξον ὃν ἐξελέξω ἐκ τούτων τῶν δύο ἕνα
1:24.targetText: And they prayed, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen

groups.note: καρδιογνῶστα ("knower of hearts") is rendered know … heart.
ὃν … ἕνα ("the one whom") is rendered which.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the praying participle as the main verb, so εἶπαν ("they said") has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the indirect object of Show; the Greek has none.

1:25.sourceText: λαβεῖν τὸν τόπον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης καὶ ἀποστολῆς, ἀφ’ ἧς παρέβη Ἰούδας πορευθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν ἴδιον.
1:25.targetText: to take up this ministry and apostleship, which Judas abandoned to go to his rightful place.”

groups.note: ἴδιον ("his own") is rendered his rightful.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB says take up this ministry, leaving τὸν τόπον τῆς ("the place of") without English words.
The preposition ἀπό ("from") is absorbed into the English verb abandoned.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:26.sourceText: καὶ ἔδωκαν κλήρους αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Μαθθίαν, καὶ συνκατεψηφίσθη μετὰ τῶν ἕνδεκα ἀποστόλων.
1:26.targetText: Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("for them") unexpressed.
